tasks.short: Chase sections and sign the pack as ready

steps.what: Name each section, its owner and its date
Open the section status for this pack
Remind owners whose section is late
Review a returned section for the pack
Comment on a technical section
Sign the regulatory pack version as ready

tasks.design: Owners submit section id, document version, owner and due date on a {WORKFLOW} form. The old chase list on a {SPREADSHEET}, fed by {EMAIL}, becomes a status view in {DOCS}. A late section gets a fixed reminder that names only the section id and the date. The specialist signs one pack version as ready. This task does not post the pack to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Section status lived in mail and a spreadsheet, so nobody could see which version had been accepted into the pack.
tasks.enabler_now: A section can be a row with an owner, a due date and a received flag, so the status view is a query rather than a rewrite.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a returned section is good enough for the pack is still a reading, not a flag.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts or returns a section and is the only person who marks the pack ready.

ambition.what: Accept or return a section on the day it arrives, not at the pack meeting

tasks.altitude: Chasing late sections is a status view. The specialist keeps the right to return a section and to withhold the ready mark.

reach.task: Comment on a technical section before the pack is marked ready
reach.learn: Which section versions are in the signed ready pack

evidence.claim: Coordinating a regulatory pack is mostly a list of sections, owners and dates, plus a reading of what comes back. The external filing is a later task.
Digest [S14] says a regulatory-information product tracks registrations and publishes submissions. That supports a status list of document versions, not a judgement that a section is good enough.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when a pack version is signed as ready or a section is returned. Posting to a portal is a separate submission task, despite the external-reach prior.

Input contract: pack id, section id, document version, owner, due date, received flag. Producer is the project lead for the plan and the section owner for the file. A row with no owner or no section id is rejected and not chased by hand. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.

The model prior is low because status is a query. The reminder text is one fixed sentence plus section id and due date, with no file contents. Test native {WORKFLOW} status and reminders before any custom code.
unknowns: Which section types are required for each pack.
Who may mark a pack ready when the specialist is absent.
Whether late reminders should go to a deputy as well as the owner.
research_questions: What share of sections arrive after the due date?
How often does the specialist return a section that the status view showed as received?

already_counted.description: Specialist reading time on a returned section
Ready signature stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a section type when a new pack shape appears
Owners resubmit a section the specialist returned

approvals.approved_version: pack version signed as ready in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes section files still arrive as unnamed mail, so the status view stays empty and the specialist still chases by hand. The high case assumes clean rows but every returned section and the ready signature stay with the specialist. Portal filing is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and sign a response to an agency request

steps.what: Log each question the agency asked
Attach the source document for each question
Draft the response from those source documents

loop.input: sourced questions and the response template
loop.output: draft whose paragraphs cite source document ids
loop.check: Each paragraph cites a source document id the project lead named
loop.stop: Leave the paragraph blank and stop if the question has no source document id
loop.why_not_simpler: The answer wording is not a fixed sentence stored on the question

steps.what: Sign the regulatory response version
File only the signed response version

tasks.design: The specialist logs each agency question id, the document asked for and the due date from {EMAIL} onto a {WORKFLOW} form. The project lead attaches a source document id per question. A draft in {DOCS} may use only those sources. The specialist signs one response version. Only that version is filed through {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency questions and the answers were spread across mail threads, so a response could not show which source it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Each question can carry a source document id, so a paragraph without that id can be dropped.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the source actually answers the question is a judgement, and a filed response is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides the answer is sufficient and signs the only version that may be filed.

ambition.what: Sign a response as soon as the source documents are in, instead of holding every question for a monthly pack

tasks.altitude: Drafting from named sources takes less rewriting. The specialist can refuse a response that does not answer the question.

reach.task: Attach the source document the question names
reach.learn: Which questions already have a signed response and which are still open

evidence.claim: A further-information response is a letter tied to source documents. The specialist still decides whether the source answers the question.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so each response paragraph must cite a source document id the project lead named.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed response version is filed or the specialist refuses it. The spoken agency exchange is a separate task.

Input contract: question id, due date, document asked, source document id, source version. Producer of the question row is the specialist from the mailbox. Producer of the source document id is the project lead. A question with no source document id is not drafted. If the mail has no question id the specialist types one and marks the row manual.
Test native {DOCS} templates, {WORKFLOW} fields and the approval flow before any custom code. A machine may file only the signed response version.
unknowns: Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
How long the firm keeps the source documents.
research_questions: What share of agency questions arrive with no identifiable document ask?
How often does the specialist reject the first draft for a missing source?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits paragraphs that do not answer the question
Signature time on the response stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Revise the response template when a new question shape appears
Project leads replace a source document the draft rejected

approvals.approved_version: response version signed for this question set

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes questions stay as unstructured mail and source ids are missing, so the specialist still assembles the response by hand. The high case assumes named sources but every sufficiency call and every signature stays with the specialist. The agency conversation is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide the submission type for a device or label change

steps.what: Submit the device or labeling change fields
Return the matching submission-type row
Decide the submission or document type
Write the signed type onto the change
Read the type before work continues

tasks.design: The product owner submits change kind, product id, market, whether intended use changed, whether label text changed and whether a component was added, on a {WORKFLOW} form. A table in {DOCS} returns the matching submission type or internal document type, or an empty row. The specialist accepts or overrides that row and signs the decision. Nothing is sent to {GOV_PORTAL} from this task. A {SPREADSHEET} of past decisions is not the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change descriptions arrived as prose in mail, so two similar device or labeling changes were classified differently with no row to compare.
tasks.enabler_now: The change can be coded fields, so a matching row is a lookup and an empty row is a visible miss.
tasks.still_hard: A change that does not match a row, or that sits on a boundary, is still the specialist's call. A wrong type is costly to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts or overrides the submission type and will not let an empty row be treated as a decision.

ambition.what: Give a submission-type decision for every device or labeling change in the week it is proposed

tasks.altitude: Looking up a known change takes less time. The specialist can override the row and can refuse to decide when a field is blank.

reach.task: Stop work that the signed type does not allow
reach.learn: Which change ids have a signed submission type and which are still blank

evidence.claim: Choosing a submission or document type for a device or labeling change is a coded lookup plus a person. A model is a poor fit once the inputs are fields, and the boundary cases stay manual.
A wrong type is a legal and financial miss that is hard to undo, so the specialist signs the decision even when the lookup returns a row.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends at the signed type on the change record. Preparing the submission itself is a separate task. The external-exposure prior is the later filing, not this decision.

Input contract: change id, change kind (device or labeling), product id, market, intended-use changed (yes or no), label text changed (yes or no), component added (yes or no). Producer is the product owner. A blank field returns an empty row and is not guessed. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.
The model prior is low and this design agrees: three to six coded fields do not need a writing loop. Test the native {WORKFLOW} form and the {DOCS} table before any custom code.
unknowns: Which change kinds the firm actually uses.
Who may sign a type decision when the specialist is absent.
Whether some markets have no row in the table yet.
research_questions: What share of changes match a row on the first try?
How often does the specialist override the matched row?

already_counted.description: Override and signature time stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a row when a new change kind has no match
Product owners resubmit a change whose fields were blank

approvals.approved_version: submission type signed for this change id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most changes still arrive as free text, so the lookup returns empty and the specialist classifies by hand. The high case assumes coded fields but every type decision is still signed. Building the later submission is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the technical file and sign its version

steps.what: Register the document version for this component
Compare sections with the required list
Build the file index from current versions
Sign this technical-file version
Store the signed file in the record
File the signed version when it says submit

tasks.design: The product owner registers component id, section id, document id, version and effective date on a {WORKFLOW} form. A {DOCS} template builds the technical-file index from current versions and leaves a gap where a version is missing. The old index on a {SPREADSHEET} is not the record. The specialist signs one file version. A machine stores it, and files it through {GOV_PORTAL} only when that signature says submit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical-file indexes were recopied, and an older document could be included because the version was not a field.
tasks.enabler_now: Each section can carry a document version and an effective date, so a gap is a missing row rather than a reread of the whole file.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the file is complete enough to sign, and whether this version should be submitted, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the file version and is the only person who can mark it submit.

ambition.what: Re-sign the technical file when a component version changes, not only at the approval renewal

tasks.altitude: Index upkeep shrinks to gaps and signatures. The specialist can hold a file that is current internally and not yet submitted.

reach.task: Register a new component version before the index is rebuilt
reach.learn: Which sections are current and whether the signed version says submit or hold

evidence.claim: Maintaining a technical file is mostly version bookkeeping plus a signature. The index can be built from current rows. Completeness is still a person call.

Digest [S14] says a regulatory-information product tracks registrations and publishes submissions. That supports a versioned technical-file index and a publish of a signed version, not a judgement that the file is complete.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task maintains the technical file and, only when the signature says submit, files that version. A submission cover note is a separate task.

Input contract: file id, component id, section id, document id, version, effective date. Producer is the product owner. A section with no version stays a gap and is not filled with an older document. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.

The model prior is low. The index is a merge of current versions into the template, not a generated narrative. Test native {DOCS} templates and {WORKFLOW} fields before any custom code. The portal step runs only for a signature that says submit.
unknowns: Which sections the firm requires in a technical file.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
Which files are held for inspection rather than submitted.
research_questions: What share of sections have no current version?
How often is a signed file marked hold rather than submit?

already_counted.description: Specialist reviews gaps in the index before signing
Signature time, including the submit or hold mark, stays here

incremental.description: Add a required section when a new product type appears
Product owners register a version the gap list rejected

approvals.approved_version: technical-file version signed as hold or submit
the same signed technical-file version marked submit

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many documents are still unregistered, so the index stays full of gaps and the specialist still hunts versions by hand. The high case assumes registered versions but every signature stays manual. Unregistered documents are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week moves from chasing sections and rebuilding technical files to deciding the submission type and signing the versions other people will use.
reach: Project leads see which sections are in, late or returned.
Product owners receive a signed submission type before they change a device or a label.
Quality reviewers comment on a section before the pack is marked ready.
skills_to_grow: Run a section list as fields with an owner and a due date.
Draft an agency response only from a named source document.
Choose a submission type from coded change fields, and override the row when it does not fit.
Keep a technical file as versions, and send it out only when the sign-off says submit.
role.ambitious_version: A device or labeling change opens with a signed submission type, a current technical-file index and a pack the specialist has marked ready.
